children: Iraq and Turkey have moved a step closer to launching the $17-billion development road which they expect to turn them into a major business hub.

After marathon meetings over the past week, the two sides completed the final draft for the execution of the project which involves the construction of a 1,200 km rail and a parallel motorway from South Iraq to the Northern border with Turkey.

Representatives from the ministries of transport, oil, finance and foreign affairs as well as the State Organisation for Marketing Oil (SOMO) attended the talks with a Turkish delegation, the transport ministry said in a weekend statement.

"The discussions focused on finalising the legal, technical, and financial aspects and identifying implementation mechanisms to ensure clear mutual obligations and rights, as well as the requirements of the targeted projects between the two countries,” it said.
Besides Iraq and Turkey, the UAE and Qatar are partners in the project, the first phase of which is expected to be completed in 2029.
(Writing by N Saeed; Editing by Anoop Menon)
